newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan vice president offers goodwill visit to HK.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan vice president offers goodwill visit to HK.

text.p: Taiwan Vice President Lien Chan said on Monday he was willing to make a good-will visit to Hong Kong after it comes under the sovereignty of communist China, Taiwan's arch rival, aides said.

"The premier said he is willing to visit Hong Kong to show our good intentions," an official in the cabinet spokesman's office told Reuters by telephone. Lien doubles as vice president and premier, or cabinet chief.
Lien felt an offer to visit Hong Kong might be regarded as "less sensitive" in Beijing's eyes than a visit to the communist mainland, the official said.
No Taiwan officials were attending Hong Kong's handover ceremony, although Koo Chen-fu, head of a state-funded body formed to handle contacts with Beijing, was attending as Taipei's representative.
Lien and President Lee Teng-hui have repeatedly expressed a willingness to travel to the mainland for contacts with the Communist Party leadership, but Beijing has never given a positive response.

Beijing has regarded Nationalist-ruled Taiwan as a renegade province since a 1949 civil war split and rejects Taipei's call for government-to-government contacts on an equal footing, saying that only party-to-party contacts would be appropriate.

An angry Beijing froze what had been slowly warming semi-official talks in mid-1995 in response to a visit to the United States by Lee, which it saw as a move toward Taiwan independence and away from unification with the mainland.
